The audit repairs high-impact entities such as Kaylani Lei and Eva Lin, preserves performer-identification uncertainty, records Asa's repeated lap-dance refusals and David's immediate no during the Kira story, and keeps every offensive or contradictory idea literal while separating uncertainty, safety, consent and publication handling.
source_notes: The raw file contains 2,112 segments and approximately 12,739 words; the clean file contains 2,110 segments and the same approximate word count across 3,961.18 seconds.
Both cleaner removals are empty zero-duration artifacts at 1,080.58 and 1,219.02 seconds. No spoken idea is removed.

Repair `go get some kids` to `go get some sun` in the tanning context and `been gambled` to `haven't gambled` in the recovery statement. Leave the corrupt room-temperature and `mass ignoring` phrases uncertain pending audio verification.
The existing global `the Bellagio` to `Bellagio` proposal is rejected. Spoken phrases such as `at the Bellagio` are grammatical and literal; normalization would add no retrieval value.

In the Wicked/Las Vegas performer context, `Kehlani` is almost certainly Kaylani Lei, not the singer. `Evelyn` refers back to Episode 108 guest Eva Lin. Both repairs are contextual, never global identity merges.
The Kira Kenner identification emerges only after Kobe Tai, Kina/Kira Kai and other guesses. Preserve the search sequence and normalize only after the cast resolves it.

Asa says at least five times that the cast will not receive lap dances, including `No`, `stop`, `not going to happen` and `no amount of money`. Friendship, payment and hypothetical reframing do not reopen consent.

In the Kira Kenner story, the narrator says a performer placed another patron's hand on his genitals and that he said no. Strip-club attendance does not authorize third-party genital contact; the cast's later legal label remains attributed.

The Eva Lin discussion contains literal period slurs, objectification and gender/orientation claims. Editorial navigation uses transgender woman and separates gender identity from sexual orientation without silently rewriting the dialogue.
Instagram likes, past appearance, attraction and reported sexual preferences do not establish Eva's interest or consent. The cast itself briefly acknowledges that she may not want sexual contact.
Tears are not suitable anal lubricant. Forceful or submissive sexual preferences require explicit, act-specific, informed and revocable consent; shame or fantasy supplies none.
The exact hotel room number, private security/fees, travel, lodging, relatives, spouses, messages, partners, workers, health and contact paths remain outside public discovery.

All eight rejected suggestions are retained in the fixture so regeneration cannot turn uncertainty into certainty, payment into consent, social engagement into permission, or offensive ideas into sanitized prose.
